text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock inched up 0.24% today to close at $478.07, capping a remarkable two-week rally of 13.2%. The move reflects the sharp rise in crude oil prices this week — U.S. oil jumped from around $98 to over $101 per barrel as Iran escalated attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil supply. Refiners like Marathon profit when crude prices rise relative to the finished products they sell (gasoline and diesel), and with U.S. refineries running at 93.5% capacity, the company is well-positioned to capture margins on higher-priced crude.

The week's gains also sit against a broader tightening in physical oil markets: analysts note that the true cost to deliver crude is running roughly $30–$40 per barrel higher than posted prices due to surging tanker rates, which compounds supply pressures from the Middle East turmoil and keeps refiners incentivized to run at high utilization rates.
